assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The period analysed is 18 Sep 2026. The headline day-level rate (76.75%) is compared with the preceding day, while the significance tests compare 17-18 Sep with the reference window 10-16 Sep.

facts.text: The card success rate on 18 Sep was 76.75%, the lowest of the 22 days shown. The median daily rate was 86.72% and the highest day was 12 Sep at 87.97%.
Across 17-18 Sep, the card success rate fell 9.24pp from 87.0% to 77.75%, compared with 10-16 Sep (7,956 attempts vs 28,445). The change is statistically and practically significant.

Kestrel Bank was the segment that concentrated the drop. Its card success rate fell from 86.87% to 57.8%, a fall of 29.07pp. Other acquirers moved by about 1.5pp or less, and none of those changes were significant (Northstar Bank -1.45pp, Meridian Bank +0.8pp, Saffron Bank -0.34pp).
Within Kestrel Bank, all three card methods fell sharply: debit cards by 30.11pp to 56.31%, credit cards by 28.71pp to 59.94%, and EMI cards by 23.87pp to 56.8%.

For Kestrel Bank cards, acquirer timeouts (ACQ_TIMEOUT) rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window). Failure codes for customer drop-off and issuer declines did not rise.
Across all card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.24 to 10.24 per 100 attempts (815 failures). No other failure code moved by more than about 0.3 per 100 attempts.

The Kestrel Bank card problem ran from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 (36 hours). The worst hour was 18 Sep 02:00 at a 36.36% success rate, against a reference of 86.87%. About 716 excess failed attempts occurred out of 2,229 affected attempts.
Across all card payments, hours from 10:00 to 23:00 (and 08:00) showed significant drops against the reference week. The worst hour of day was 12:00, down 13.64pp.
The data-quality scan found no issues for 17-18 Sep.

response.headline: Card success rate on 18 Sep was 76.75%, the lowest day in the 22-day window (median 86.72%). The drop is concentrated in Kestrel Bank, where a card problem that began on 17 Sep 10:00 ran until 18 Sep 22:00.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for their incident log for 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 and compare it with the timeout timeline. Check gateway logs for the same window.
hypotheses.rationale: The decline is concentrated in one acquirer across debit, credit and EMI cards. The only failure code that rose materially is the acquirer timeout code, and other acquirers were unaffected.
hypotheses.text: A Kestrel Bank acquirer-side technical problem, such as an outage or connectivity degradation, caused the drop.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A Kestrel Bank acquirer-side technical problem, such as an outage or connectivity degradation, caused the drop.
recommendations.rationale: Acquirer timeouts and the Kestrel-only drop point to an acquirer-side issue that needs confirmation and a fix.
recommendations.text: Raise an incident with Kestrel Bank and request a root-cause report for 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The Kestrel Bank card problem ran from 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00 (36 hours). The worst hour was 18 Sep 02:00 at a 36.36% success rate, against a reference of 86.87%. About 716 excess failed attempts occurred out of 2,229 affected attempts.
recommendations.rationale: The problem ran for 36 hours; faster detection and rerouting would limit the roughly 716 excess failed attempts.
recommendations.text: Set up a per-acquirer alert on acquirer timeout rate and hourly success rate, and consider routing card traffic to healthy acquirers during future Kestrel degradations.
